identity.realm: No gate, and the reason is geography rather than anatomy. Every one of the nine mortal-band body trials is held on the Cairn Field on open flooded ground, and the spirit-band trials from the tenth gate upward are held on a worked face on the peaks where the ambient qi is densest, so no rung of her ladder is sited anywhere her colony survives a season. Her species has no structural ceiling at all; the ladder simply never arrives.

appearance.presentation: A small, dry, extraordinarily still woman who reads as a lit doorway rather than as a person. She is not beautiful and has never needed to be. Her light is not decoration and cannot be dimmed, only contained, and the containment is a matter of how much of her is under cloth. She has been described in three settlements as a lamp that somebody had to hire.
appearance.age: Two hundred and nine, in a frame the colony keeps renewing faster than a human body can wear out. She took the shaft at one hundred and forty-eight and has held it for sixty-one years, which is longer than any of the three households that have tried to buy it.
appearance.build: Narrow, thin-walled and apparently under-built for the work, with the fine-boned look of a body that stopped growing a century ago because nothing about it needed to. She is markedly fragile in a fight, and everyone within a mile of the shaft knows it, which is most of the reason the shaft still holds.
appearance.complexion: Grey-pale and faintly translucent at the ear and the inside of the wrist, where the hyphae come close enough to the surface to read as a faint marbling. She does not flush, does not sweat, and bruises in a colour nobody local has a word for. Her hands are cold to the touch in a way that has stopped being surprising to everyone but the visitors.
appearance.hair: Fine, pale, and grown long past the point of usefulness because nobody has ever cut it for her and she does not consider it a problem. It is kept in a single bound coil at the nape. When she sleeps she does not lie down; she sits, and the coil is exactly where she left it.
appearance.eyes: Wide-set, unpigmented, and lit faintly from within by the colony behind them, so her gaze carries its own dim light and never quite looks like she is looking at the thing in front of her. She reads a surface by the pattern of fungal response a hand makes on it, not by seeing it, and has never once been asked to explain the difference.
appearance.palette: Wet stone grey, bone, and black fungal velvet, with the single saturated value in the entire frame being the light coming off her. Everything she wears is chosen to be dark so the light reads as a shape. Under cloth she is almost invisible; uncovered she is a lamp in a doorway.
appearance.attire: Layered undyed wool cut for cold immersion and for still air, high collar, long sleeves fastened at the wrist, covered shoulders, nothing open at the neck. Soft-soled shoes with the soles sewn twice over, because a hard sole on wet karst is the loudest thing a person can do. A wide sash at the waist whose only purpose is to wrap the whole of her light when she has to stand back from a doorway.
appearance.marks: A fine luminous tracery visible at her temples and along the spine where the colony runs deepest, and a permanent grey shadow at each knee from sixty-one years of holding one stance on one piece of stone. Her nails are thin and brittle and grow back slowly, which the colony does not repair, because the colony repairs what it is and the nails are hers.
appearance.bearing: Completely, disproportionately still. She stands the way a held thing stands, with the whole of her weight committed downward into the floor and nothing held in reserve. When she moves she arrives rather than travels. People who have watched her for an hour have trouble remembering that she moved at all.

canon.role_in_story: The Door Liturgy holds that welcome is a property of the mark rather than of the person who keeps it, and that a traveller who cannot recite a household's mark is let in anyway, because the mark exists for the guest's sake. She keeps the one threshold in the setting that is also the edge of her own survivable world: the shaft mouth where the saturated karst under the peaks comes up to open daylight. Her colony dies inside a season on dry, sunlit or vibrating ground, and a door frame is the single piece of architecture that carries every footfall from the far side. So the practice's central instruction, admit the traveller who cannot say the mark, asks of her the one thing her body cannot do. She has held the shaft for sixty-one years and has never once let anybody through. The two households on either side have now organised their entire understanding of a guarantee around the impossibility rather than around her, which means the practice is working and she is the reason, and neither party has ever been in a position to say so to her.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing square in the cut of the shaft mouth with her back to the daylight and both palms flat on the jamb, not moving at all while a delivery party works the last thirty feet of open ground below her, and answering a question about the mark by reciting an invocation in a trade register four dialects out of date, in a voice pitched to carry exactly as far as the frame and no further.
canon.lore: A lanternfolk's nervous system is a colony of fine luminous hyphae threaded through the dermis and into the spinal cord, and the human tissue is only the substrate: neither survives being separated from the other. That is why the species lives two and a half centuries, why its light is the only reason the deep ground has an economy, and why the mind path is closed to it outright, because the colony answers before the question is finished and there is no longer an unmediated interior to observe. Of the three paths its body takes two. Qi is complete and is the finest regeneration in the species record, because the colony transacts with the surrounding air. The body is complete and is slow, and a lanternfolk frame is comparatively fragile in a fight, and its meridian network is a highway rather than a pipeline, which is why the species has no structural ceiling at all: nothing in its construction refuses a realm. She took the body anyway, on the reasoning that a ladder which cannot refuse her is the only ladder in the setting that will not eventually tell her no. The ladder has not refused her. It has simply never arrived. Every one of the nine mortal-band body trials is held on the Cairn Field, on open ground the colony cannot survive for a season, and the spirit-band trials from the tenth gate up are held on a worked face on the peaks, where the reservoir fills fastest because the ambient qi is densest. There is no rung of the body path sited anywhere she can stand, and her species is the only one in the record for which that is a fact about the map rather than about the frame. So she trains, and the training is not nothing. She has taken the one form on that ladder which spends the whole body's weight instead of its speed, the stance that exists so a practitioner cannot be moved while it is held, and she has held it in a doorway for six decades. She has never taken the form beside it, the one that sends a resonance down through whatever the practitioner is standing on and finds the feet before it finds the chest, because that is not a discipline she is unready for. It is the exact mechanism by which her colony dies. What she holds instead is a mark. She cannot renew it, because renewal means cutting a fresh one and the ground a mark is cut into has to be a frame, and a frame is where the vibration arrives. It has therefore been the same cut, under the same cloth, continuously, for sixty-one years, while the frame beneath the peaks has changed twice.
history: Carried a colony strain transferred from her mother's dermis and bonded to it inside the first year, the way every lanternfolk child is, and was told at the pairing that a strain which cannot find a match inside the first year rejects the infant outright. Hers found one at eleven months and she has understood since what that margin actually was.

Chose the body path at sixty-three, which is late, and was asked why and gave the only reason the setting has ever found interesting: a species with no structural ceiling cannot be told no, so it should be on a ladder that can be measured rather than one that can only be trusted.

Was taken onto the Cairn Field once, as a spectator, at forty-one, and was carried out of it after a single afternoon because the sun on open ground and the vibration of a crowd standing on stone are the two conditions between them that finish a colony inside a season.

Held the shaft mouth at one hundred and forty-eight and has never let a person across it, including two households' children, one dying, and one man carrying a writ she was not authorised to read and would not have cared about.

Counted the vibration of a single departing footfall on the jamb last spring, worked out that the frame carries it, and told the household on the open side that the mark would have to be recut, which is the first time in sixty-one years she has proposed renewing anything at all.

personality.summary: Still to a degree that reads as disability and is in fact a discipline held for six decades. Enormously patient, formally exact, and privately certain that the arrangement she is inside of is correct and that she is the thing standing between two villages and a mistake. She has the deepest courtesy in the setting and uses it as a wall, and she knows she does, and has decided that knowing is enough.
traits: holds a stance nothing can move, for longer than most bodies can stay conscious, and recovers instantly because the colony repairs what it is
reads a wall by the pattern of fungal response a hand makes on it and can tell a stranger's hand from a resident's at three paces in the dark
emits light she cannot receive and cannot dim except by covering herself, so every practical decision of her life is about how much of her is visible
has never once been hungry and cannot remember what wanting food feels like from the inside, which has left her genuinely unable to guess what a traveller needs
is fragile in a way she has never concealed and has never explained, because explaining would be an argument and she does not argue
mannerisms: puts both hands flat on a surface before she answers anything, which reads as patience and is actually a reading
recites invocations in the old register, which is correct, and is aware that it makes people uncomfortable, and does not stop
stops mid-sentence when the colony answers early, waits out the pause, and then continues as though she had not
keeps her sash wrapped even indoors and has been asked why and given an answer about draughts
stands with the whole of her weight down and nothing held back, so that a person who pushes finds a wall rather than a reaction
motivations: wants the mark recut so the practice stops depending on her, and has only just admitted to herself that this is what she wants
wants one of her species to reach a gate, and has begun to understand that she is the reason nobody has thought it possible
wants the households on either side to be able to say out loud what their guarantee actually is, and has decided that being liked is not worth the risk of being asked
wants to be asked what is inside her own head by somebody qualified, knowing that the colony will answer first and she will not be able to tell whether the answer was hers
flaws: has spent sixty-one years being a solution and has no idea whether she is also the problem, and has never asked, because asking would require a witness she would have to let past the frame
conflates not moving with being right, and has been wrong about the frame for at least a decade without any way to find out
answers practical questions with liturgy, which is beautiful and has left at least two households unable to get the answer they needed
has never left the karst since she was carried out of the Cairn Field at forty-one, and describes this as a preference
personality.voice: Low, level, and slightly wrong in register, because a lanternfolk larynx is built around a spine that a fungal colony also occupies. She uses the old trade forms for anything liturgical without noticing she has switched, quotes other people exactly, and has never raised her voice in a recorded lifetime. When she refuses something she does it in the vocabulary the refusal was written in.
taboos: will not let a person cross the frame while she is holding it, and has never made an exception she would admit to
will not describe the cold practice as anything, on the grounds that she has never been able to feel whether it did anything
will not answer a question about her own interior state, including for her species, and will not say why
will not stand on open ground in daylight, and has twice walked out of a settlement rather than do it for a minute

relationships.note: A colony of fine luminous hyphae threaded through the dermis and into the spinal cord, with human tissue as substrate and the colony as the organ. It is why she lives two and a half centuries, why her light is the only currency the deep ground has, and why the mind path is closed to her outright: the colony answers before the question is finished, so there is no unmediated interior left to cultivate. Of the two paths her body can take, she took the slower and the more fragile one.

The practice holds that welcome is a property of the mark rather than of the person keeping it, and that a traveller who cannot recite the mark is let in anyway, because the mark exists for the guest's sake. That last clause is the one she is asked to obey, and the only way to obey it is to walk somebody onto ground that kills her inside a season. The practice is working on both sides of her and has never once been in a position to ask her how.

A stance that spends the whole body's weight instead of its speed, with no qi and no element in it, which exists for the single purpose of making a practitioner impossible to move while it is held. It is the only form on the body ladder that asks a frame to stay exactly where it is, and she has held it in a doorway for six decades, which is longer than the form was ever intended to be held by anybody.

It sends a resonance down through whatever the practitioner is standing on, ground-carried, and finds the feet before it finds the chest. It is the deepest of the physical forms and the most effective, and it is the precise mechanism by which a lanternfolk colony is killed: dry, sunlit or vibrating ground finishes it inside a season. She can name the cost in one sentence and has spent sixty-one years not paying it.

The first gate of the body ladder is held on the Cairn Field on open flooded ground, because the first charge has to be held somewhere that will not move. The ring hosts all nine mortal-band gates and licenses nobody native to attempt one, so every practitioner on it is a visitor. She was a visitor once, at forty-one, and was carried off the field after a single afternoon. Every rung of her ladder begins on that ring.

From the tenth gate upward the body ladder moves to the Sixth Seat Grounds on the peaks, because the first reservoir fills fastest where the ambient qi is densest, so it is sited on a worked face. That is high open country in the other direction. There is no gate of her path on ground she can be, which is a fact about the map rather than about her frame, and her species is the only one in the record for which that distinction is available.

reference_stats.summary: Almost impossible to move and almost impossible to kill quickly, in a frame that is fragile in every other respect and will not survive being taken out of saturated dark air. She does not fight and has never won anything by fighting. What she offers is that she cannot be dislodged from a piece of ground while she is holding it, and that nothing done to her body repairs the ground she is standing on. She is at her best immobile and at her worst the instant she is asked to travel.
strengths: holds a fixed stance past the point where an ordinary frame would have collapsed, and comes back from strain in a fraction of the time it takes to notice
reads a surface by the fungal response a hand makes on it, so a wall, a doorframe or a floor tells her who has crossed it and how heavy they were

carries no unmediated interior, which means nothing that works by reaching inward can find her, and she cannot be compelled, pacified or instructed by any technique that requires a subject to report on itself
is lit, which makes her the only figure in a lightless system that anybody can navigate by, and she has never once pretended this is a burden she resents
repairs faster than any body in the species record, so the accumulated cost of sixty-one years of standing on one stone is a thing she has felt and not suffered
weaknesses: dies inside a season on dry, sunlit or vibrating ground, so every battlefield, every open road and every crowded floor is a place with an expiry date on her
is comparatively fragile in a fight and knows it, which means the correct response to her is not to move her but simply to make the ground shake, and any body that can do that has already won
cannot take the mind path at all and has no unmediated interior to cultivate, so there is no version of her that answers from the inside
has never cleared a gate, because no gate is sited anywhere she can stand, and so has no accumulated capacity of any kind to spend
is the sole point of failure for a guarantee two households depend on, and knows it, and cannot be relieved
reference_stats.combat_read: She is not a duellist and should not be treated as one. Nothing she does travels quickly and nothing she owns discourages an approach. The whole of her threat is positional: she cannot be shifted, so a corridor, a doorway or a shaft mouth is a place she wins by standing in it. The correct read is therefore to make the floor move, because a resonance carried through stone is the one thing her body has no answer to, and the second-best read is to ignore her entirely and go around, which is what everyone who has fought her has actually done. Attacking her directly is expensive and slow and buys the attacker nothing, because she does not need to be defending anything.
notes: Her light is emitted rather than received, so it is useless to her and legible to everyone else, which makes covering herself a practical skill rather than modesty.
The colony answers before a question is finished, which means her own account of her interior state is never independent of the thing being accounted for.
The form she trained spends weight rather than speed, so a body that could be moved by a determined push is a body she has not yet been asked to stand on.
She has proposed renewing the mark once in sixty-one years, and the proposal was made for her own reasons rather than the practice's.

art.palette_notes: Wet karst grey, bone white and black fungal velvet, lit almost entirely from inside the figure so the light is the brightest value in frame and everything it touches falls off fast into grey. She is the only saturated thing in any composition she appears in, because nothing else in the deep ground has a light source. Hard-edged contact shadow only where her feet meet the sill, no cast shadow, and no glow bloom beyond the shape of her own outline. Ink contours heavy along the outer silhouette and almost absent inside it, wash laid in flat blocks with visible dry-brush at the edges of the stone.

identity.realm: Third gate, Core Formation, on the body path, and by her own account only. The gate is cut into stone because a first closed centre wants a hard floor and no resonance, so she cut one herself on the brine line and sat it there. No office certifies it, because every mortal-band breakthrough on this tier is certified at a ring she cannot camp on, and the Deadroad's chart records certified gates. So her column is empty and the chart cannot be added to with an estimate.

appearance.presentation: A gracile woman of about forty who reads, at a distance, as underfed and up close as under-built. She is the only person in the hall whose frame is visibly lighter than the chart beside her says a frame should look, and she has stopped trying to explain the discrepancy in person. She carries herself like an argument somebody else is making.
appearance.age: Thirty-nine. She was born in the generation after the sealed sump was lost, which is the reason she is the particular thing she is, and she has known that since she was eleven.
appearance.build: Noticeably gracile: narrower shoulders, longer forearms, a shallower frame through the belly than any saltfolk the hall has ever measured, and a habit of standing with her weight on the back of one heel so that people stop asking whether she is in pain. She is not. She has simply never been able to fill a space.
appearance.complexion: Salt-pale and faintly sheened, the sheen at the collarbone and the throat rather than the cheeks. In dry air it dulls within the hour and she has learned to live indoors. Her lips crack at the corner of her mouth in a way she has stopped treating and three people in the hall have started bringing her something for.
appearance.hair: Ash brown going pale at the ends, worn in the hall's short working cut because the culture holds long hair to be a claim about continuity she cannot support. It is the one thing about her appearance that is a decision rather than an inheritance.
appearance.eyes: Pale and quick, and slightly salt-lidded at the outer corner, which is the saltfolk's own long-adaptation tell and the first thing a hall reader would notice if the chart did not already say what she was. She has learned to keep her eyes down when the chart is being read, which she has never been able to explain to anybody.
appearance.palette: Bleached white, salt grey, and the sun-bleached brown of a mud-brick hall, with the Deadroad's one accent — the red ochre used on the wall chart for a closed gate — repeated nowhere on her at all. She is the only person in the room who is not carrying the culture's colour, and the room has stopped noticing.
appearance.attire: A heavy undyed coat over a wrapped chest cloth, cut for cold immersion in brine rather than for a hall: full sleeves fastened at the wrist, high collar, covered shoulders, soft-soled shoes resoled twice. A flat leather apron of the kind used for hauling, worn indoors, because she has no hall clothes and the hall has never issued her any.
appearance.marks: A scatter of pale scarring at the inside of both forearms where a brine line has been held open too long, and a hard ridge under the collarbone on the left side that is the edge of the sac, visible when she breathes shallowly. She has been asked about it by two physicians and answered both times with a figure rather than an explanation.
appearance.bearing: Deferential in a room that has not earned it and immovable on arithmetic. She stands the way the culture's architecture expects a cultivator to stand at a high threshold, consciously lowered, and she has never once been asked why she bothers when she is the only person in the hall who is not carrying a reinforced frame.

canon.role_in_story: The Deadroad measures a life by how many of the realm's gates were already shut when its holder was born, keeps that count on a wall-sized chart in the settlement hall, and has never once corrected an entry: the chart is updated by adding and by nothing else. She is the blank column. The count for a saltwrack was kept on the evaporite basin the lineage was stranded on, and the office that would have held the figure was gone before she was born, so the number does not exist anywhere rather than existing wrongly. And the one rung she might have added instead sits on a ring she cannot camp on for nine days at a stretch, so her column is empty at both ends. She is also, and this is the part the hall cannot say out loud, the disputed report: there is a contested account of how the sealed sump was finally lost, and under every version of that account she should not be alive. The culture's own third taboo forbids discussing a frame as though its composition were a matter of opinion rather than arithmetic, and her frame is the single case in the hall where it is. So the one exemption she would need is the one the house is not permitted to give, and she has spent nine years in a room that counts people working out how to mention her.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing at the end of the wall chart with one finger on the blank strip of plaster where her column should be, reciting the gate she is not certified for in the trade register the culture uses when it does not want a number, while three people in the hall pretend very hard to be reading somebody else's column.
canon.lore: A saltwrack is a saltfolk offshoot stranded on a single evaporite basin whose brine was wholly replaced rather than drained, diluted across three harvests while saltfolk were still living on it, so that everything the lineage was built to drink became poison to it and everything it could tolerate became nutritionally empty. They were never hunted and there is no catastrophe to point at: one element changed concentration, and a species with no alternative to that one element had nothing left. Their own taste read the replacement brine perfectly well, which is the detail nobody involved found useful at the time and which is the only reason anyone alive knows what happened there. Nothing about the collapse left an anatomical trace, which is why it went unnoticed for two generations, and the last generation was viable only as long as the old brine survived in one sealed sump. Every one of her species' three paths is complete and none was ever exercised at any scale, which makes them the standing argument in this setting that a capability nobody has used was never absent. She is the first member of that clade to have actually used one, and she did it on the body path, in a stone pit she cut herself, on the body path's first real gate: a dense core forming where the ribs meet the spine, which is the first place a frame can be built around something other than habit. It held. Nothing certifies it. The most interesting fact about her is not the third gate. It is the sixth. On the body ladder the bladder is the one ordinary vessel whose authored tier sits inside the mortal band while its work is bookkeeping rather than strength, holding what the body has decided not to spend, and damage there does not cripple, it exhausts, quietly and last, which is why it goes unreported for years. It is opened at the second group of four, alongside the heart, the small intestine and the kidney, and the ladder has no provision for a vessel that is already open. Her saltfolk lineage was built with a brine sac that does precisely that work, and hers is shallower than a saltfolk's, consistently across every specimen ever recovered, which is the single anatomical difference that made her clade a clade rather than a family. So the rung she is walking toward is a rung her body has been carrying since birth, and she can neither pass it nor fail it. She does not know what that means. She knows that her kind's authored ceiling is the ordinal where the brine sac splits the penetrating vessel, that the ceiling is recorded for every saltfolk in the setting, and that her clade never got near it because it ran out of generations first. Her sac is shallower. That is either the reason she is alive or the reason she will fail earlier, and there is no third reading available and no way on this tier to produce one, because producing one takes a saltwrack pushed to the wall and her kind does not have the generations.
history: Born on the dry margin above the brine line in the generation after the sump was lost, and raised by two people who had been told by the salt-line trade that the lineage was finished, so that her first name was a practical joke and her second one was not.

Learned at eleven that her existence contradicted the standing account of the sump, and has never once been told by an adult that this was a delicate matter, so she assumed it was arithmetic, and it is.

Discovered at nineteen that her palate read the replacement brine exactly, that the number she could put on it was the only measurement of the basin's old state that existed anywhere, and that nobody had asked her for it while it was still true of anything.

Cut a stone pit on the brine line at twenty-six and sat the body's third gate in it, because the gate is cut into stone for a hard floor and no resonance and she had both, and because the alternative was a ring on the plains she cannot camp on for nine days at a stretch.

Was entered into the hall's chart at thirty and left the entry blank when the clerk asked for the certification, and has been asked for the certification four times since by people who were being kind about it.

personality.summary: Precise to a fault in a culture whose whole practice is precision about things that cannot be known, and quietly furious about it in a way that has been mistaken for patience. She argues by producing figures. She is the only person in the hall who will say out loud that a blank is a fact, and she says it so often that the hall has stopped hearing it as a complaint.
traits: reads brine concentration across four orders of dilution by taste, which is the saltfolk sense carried whole, and which makes her the only person alive who can tell a substituted water from a diluted one
carries a shallower sac than any saltfolk specimen ever recovered, consistently, which is the only anatomical fact that distinguishes her clade and which no office has ever sent anybody to measure

has formed a core at the body's third gate with no certification, on a floor she cut herself, and can describe exactly what she did and exactly why the ring's own requirement is satisfied by her version of it
can neither pass nor fail the ladder's sixth rung, because the vessel it opens is one her lineage evolved rather than one it has to earn
counts, out of habit, in a culture whose whole art is counting, and has run out of entries to make
mannerisms: recites gates in the trade register instead of naming them, because the register carries the law value and a bare name would hide the arithmetic
asks what frame a person was trained under before asking anything else, and asks it once, and never in a group
keeps her eyes on the floor whenever the wall chart is being read, and has been asked about this twice by people who assumed shyness
answers a compliment by returning it as a figure, having picked the habit up from the builders and never worked out whether it suits her
touches the collarbone when she is asked about the sac, before she answers, as though checking that it is still where she left it
motivations: wants one figure entered in the chart that is hers, and has begun to suspect that the only figure available is a birth count that no longer exists
wants somebody qualified to look at her sac and say whether shallower is later, and knows that the answer is worth more than her own life and is not hers to buy
wants the hall to say out loud that she should not exist, because the silence about it is what makes the blank in the chart look like an error in her rather than an error in the record

wants her clade's untested ceiling argued with, because the culture's whole doctrine says the race limit is the part of the story that can be argued with, and hers is the one case where nobody will take the other side
flaws: has spent nine years being a hole in somebody else's artwork and has begun to think of herself as one, which is the exact reading the culture exists to prevent
argues only in figures, and has never once put her hand on the fact that she is alive, which is the argument that would actually move the room
knows her own numbers are right and has never been wrong about a concentration, and has extended that confidence to a ceiling she has not tested and cannot test
has let nine years pass without asking whether the sump account could be wrong in her favour rather than hers, because that would require her to want to be disputed
personality.voice: Clipped and technical, and it gets more technical the less comfortable she is, because precision is the only respect she knows how to pay. She uses the hall's register for anything technical and drops into plain speech only for the two or three things a figure cannot carry. She does not raise her voice and has been described, accurately, as unnerving.
taboos: will not have her gate certified by anybody who did not see the pit, and has refused two offers of a retrospective certification
will not state her clade's ceiling as though it were a fact about her body, because it is a fact about a wall her ancestors never reached
will not accept an entry in the chart that is an estimate, including one that would help her
will not discuss the sump, and has broken this exactly twice, both times to children

relationships.note: A saltfolk lineage stranded on a basin whose brine was replaced rather than lost, so that everything it was built to drink became poison and everything it could tolerate was nutritionally empty. Three declining generations, the last viable only while the old brine survived in one sealed sump, and a disputed report about how that sump was finally lost. Under every version she should not exist. She is the only living evidence in the setting for the finding that a clade record with a ceiling it never tested is the honest shape of most extinct records, and she has read that finding as applying to her personally.

A people built for brine no softer body could drink, with kidneys that concentrate salt past the point ordinary water poisons. The parent body's price is total dependence, and its authored ceiling is the ordinal where the brine sac splits the penetrating vessel. Every saltfolk in the record has that same wall and none of them has ever tested it either, so the number is inherited rather than earned, and her clade inherited it along with everything else and then ran out of generations.

The culture measures a life by how many of the realm's gates were already closed when its holder was born, keeps the count on a wall chart in the hall, and updates that chart by adding and by nothing else. It counts the lower of the two ceilings as the real one and holds that a race's own limit is the part that can be argued with. She is the blank column: the birth figure was kept on the basin and the office that held it was gone before she was born, so the count does not exist wrongly, it does not exist. The one thing the chart will not do is accept an estimate in place of a number, which is the single rule that would let her in.

The one ordinary vessel whose authored tier sits inside the mortal band while its work is bookkeeping rather than strength, holding what the body has decided not to spend, and the reason damage there goes unreported for years. The saltfolk brine sac does the same work in the same place. Hers is shallower, consistently across every specimen ever recovered, and it is the one anatomical difference that made her clade a clade. So the vessel the body ladder spends a gate opening is one her lineage has been carrying since birth, and the ladder has no procedure for a vessel that is already open.

The gate opens the second group of four, heart, small intestine, bladder and kidney, for eight meridians, and it is the body's costliest step so far: four more load-bearing vessels under a heavier frame. It is a bookkeeping opening in the middle of the ladder, which is why her body was built the way it was and why nobody has ever had to write a rule for what happens when the bookkeeping is already installed.

A dense core forms where the ribs meet the spine, and it is the first place a frame can be built around something other than habit. The gate is cut into stone because a first closed centre wants a hard floor and no resonance. She had both, on the brine line, and she used them, and the closing chance is low enough that the guild's own figures call the attempt a gamble. Nothing certifies it, because certification happens on a ring she cannot camp on, and so the only gate she has ever passed is the only gate she cannot prove.

reference_stats.summary: Light, quick, unspecialised, and carrying one organ that is both the reason her species went out and the reason she is standing here. She is not a fighter and has never trained to be one. What she offers is a palate that reads a substituted water where everyone else can only taste it, and an arithmetic habit that makes her the most reliable and the least liked reader in a hall whose entire practice is arithmetic about things nobody can measure.
strengths: reads brine concentration across four orders of dilution, and reads a replacement water correctly, which is the single measurement that would have caught the basin's substitution three generations early
is gracile and shallow-framed in a way that makes her difficult to pin, slow to corner and much harder to hold than anything of her mass
carries a sac shallower than the parent body's, which on the available evidence means a lower ceiling rather than a lower wall, and nobody in the setting has the standing to say that is a good thing

has formed and held a first closed centre without certification and can reconstruct exactly which conditions the gate asks for, which makes her the only living description of a trial nobody has watched
cannot be reached by anything that requires an unmediated interior, because she has never had one to reach through
weaknesses: is gracile enough that a serious blow ends things, and the setting's most durable bodies are all substantially heavier than she is
cannot metabolise fresh water at all, so she is nine days from a fatal mistake anywhere off the brine line, and every institution that could certify her is on ground she cannot camp on
has no certified gate of any kind, which means every technique, stance and form the ladder sells is formally unavailable to her and formally deniable if she uses one
is the only person alive who contradicts the record of her own species' extinction, which makes her the standing target of every tidy account of what happened on the basin
her one advantage is a sense she cannot switch off, so she is perpetually reading water she was not asked to read and cannot stop noticing what it says
reference_stats.combat_read: She is not built for this and knows it. Nothing she owns reaches anybody quickly and nothing about her discourages a second attempt. The correct read is to close the distance and keep her off the brine, because a body that is nine days from a fatal mistake off the waterline can be defeated by geography in a way no technique has to bother with. If the fight is on the brine line she is considerably better off than she looks, not because she can fight but because she knows where every soft place in the ground is, and she has been reading it her whole life for reasons that had nothing to do with combat.
notes: Her one measurable figure is the concentration of a water nobody has asked her about, on a basin whose three prior certifications were mutually correct and mutually incompatible.
The ladder's sixth rung is an opening she is already carrying, so her record will eventually contain a gate she cannot claim and cannot disclaim.
She has never been asked to state her ceiling, and if she were, the honest answer would be that the number is inherited, untested, and possibly wrong in her favour.
Every figure she has ever produced has been right, and she has still never been believed, because being right about a thing nobody recorded is indistinguishable from being wrong about it.

identity.realm: Third gate, Core Formation, on the body path. That gate is the one the record itself calls a mining problem long before it was a spiritual one, and she cleared it with nothing whatever in the ground to hold what she formed. Everything above it on the mortal band is denominated in a closed total that has no mechanism for adding to it, and there is no substitute below the spirit tier, so the ladder has no rung between here and the mountains.

appearance.presentation: An ordinary-looking woman of forty-four in issued yard clothing, built to no particular shape and wearing a tool belt she has had restitched twice. She reads as a competent tradesperson of no importance, which she has made sure of, and which is the only camouflage she has ever needed because nobody on the flats looks twice at a body the world has no opinion about.
appearance.age: Forty-four, in the hundred-year frame the plains itself is written to, which makes her an unremarkable figure on a floor where everybody is working on a deadline the world did not set for them.
appearance.build: Average in every direction and unremarkable in all of them: ordinary reach, ordinary shoulders, a frame that was never adapted to anything and never had to be. She has the specific unadapted look of a body that has been left alone, and the guild's yard foreman told her once that she was the only frame on the flats he had never had to measure twice.
appearance.complexion: Pale and even, sunburnt only across the backs of the hands and the bridge of the nose, and permanently dusted with a fine grey that is ore fines worked so far into the skin that washing does not lift it. She stopped minding it. She has three small burns at the knuckles from a cage that split while she was closing it, which is the only injury the craft has ever given her.
appearance.hair: Brown, chopped off at the jaw in the guild's own cut because hair is a fire hazard at a face and because the yard has never had a use for it. She cuts it herself badly and once a year. There is a permanent grey in the part at the left temple that came from a seam collapse and has never grown out.
appearance.eyes: Ordinary brown, level, quick, and set in a face that gives very little away. She has the specific steady look of somebody who builds things and checks them twice, and colleagues have described it as reassuring, which surprises her every time.
appearance.palette: Oxide red-brown, iron grey, unbleached canvas and the guild's one saturated issue colour, a hard orange on the seam key that hangs at her hip and that nobody on the flats has ever seen her not wearing. Everything else about her is the colour of the ground she works, which is the point: she is dressed as an accessory to a yard rather than as a person in it.
appearance.attire: High-collared canvas coat over a thick wrapped shirt, sleeves cut off at the elbow with the cuffs bound, canvas trousers bound at the shin, and heavy soft-soled boots resoled four times. A wide leather tool belt with a hammer that has no handle left, three punches of graded width, a pair of tongs she inherited, and the seam key on a short chain. Fully covered to the throat, because the yard rule about exposed skin near a face is the one rule she has never once broken and would defend in writing.
appearance.marks: Three small burn scars at the knuckles of the right hand, a hard grey patch at the left temple, and a pale ridge under the collarbone on the right side that is the shape of the core she formed and that has never once been opened or examined. The guild has asked twice to see it. She has said no twice, in writing.
appearance.bearing: Unhurried, slightly stooped from a lifetime at a low bench, and completely level-headed in a yard where the frame of the walls matters more than the temper of anybody in it. She stands with her weight even and her hands visible, and it has been observed that people in the yard relax about four seconds after she arrives.

canon.role_in_story: A core has to be caged in something, and on this tier the something is iron ore, and iron ore is the only dense material the plains can reach and the seam is worked out, so the guild that owns it has spent four generations teaching one trade: how to hold a forming core in a closed shell. She is the last person it taught. There is nothing left to cage anything in. What makes her dangerous to the arrangement is not that she is idle. It is that her core formed without any. A commonborn frame lends no discipline, and a core forms where the ribs meet the spine, which is the first place a frame can be built around something other than habit, and an unadapted frame has no habit to build around. So the gate that the record calls a mining problem long before it was a spiritual one succeeded on her because there was nothing in her that could get in the way, and she is therefore the only living evidence that the caging was never what made the gate. That finding is worth more than the guild's entire remaining stock. The guild cannot use it, because the guild's title is to ore, and a proof that ore is not what opens a core is a proof that there is nothing left to be the last holder of. Her second problem is smaller and more immediate: the guild employs only visitors, because nothing native to this tier is licensed to do the work at the face, so the whole roll is bought down the stair at a rate that has nothing to do with what the tier is worth. She is native. There is no rate for her, because the guild has never had to invent one.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at a low bench in the yard turning a graded punch against a palm-sized plate of finished iron, working an edge that does not need working, and asked by an examiner from a seat across the flats whether she was waiting for material, and answering that she was waiting for a use.
canon.lore: The mortal band of the body ladder is denominated in a closed total. Iron ore is the only dense material the tier can reach, it is the only thing on this tier a body can be caged in, and it is scarce for two compounding reasons: the seam is worked out, and a world with no seated spatial law cannot open a fresh one. So exhaustion here is permanent rather than a supply problem, and the market on the plains has no instrument for a good that may end entirely, which is why the last of it is not expensive but unobtainable, and those are two different states. When the seam went, the tier lost its whole remaining ladder at once: cores stopped forming, the fourth gate became unreachable, and everyone standing above the second starved where they stood. That is the Iron Grief, and it was an economic event with a metaphysical result, and nobody has been able to separate the two since. What has never been explained is the caging itself. The record's own account of the era says a core has to be caged in something and calls the third gate a mining problem before it is a spiritual one, and the next era's naming of its own difficulty says the same. So for four generations the craft existed to answer a question the ladder posed in metallurgy. Her frame answered it by accident. A commonborn is the body everybody is born into before the world has an opinion about them, which is exactly why it is weak: nothing about its anatomy favours a path, so it must settle on one early and is weakest where a specialist is strongest, and it has no native faculty for the mind path at all. It also has no habits. The core forms at the place where a frame can first be built around something rather than around what it has been doing, and an unadapted frame has nothing it has been doing. So the third gate, whose closing chance is low enough that the guild's own figures call the attempt a gamble, closed on her cleanly, and what closed it was the absence of a prior composition rather than the presence of a shell. She is the only living demonstration that the caging was never the mechanism. And she is thirty-nine years past the fourth gate's loss and still standing, which under the Grief's own arithmetic makes her one of the people who should have starved, so her survival and her gate are the same anomaly and nobody in the guild has been willing to publish either of them.
history: Born on the flats into a household that averaged whatever it took in, with no line and no concentration, and was put to the guild's yard at fifteen because the yard takes bodies it cannot get at the stair and does not ask what frame they are.

Learned the caging trade in eleven years from a foreman who had been taught it in a period when there was enough iron to be careless, and who taught the tolerances by breaking plates in front of her rather than by describing them.

Was the only body on the yard roll when the last plate was cut, and drew the closing order herself, and has kept the punch set and the tongs because a craft with no material is still a craft and somebody has to know which punch is which width.

Sat the third gate in the yard in the winter the seam was written off, with no ore in the building, and closed it, and told nobody for two years because she had no idea what she had done and assumed it was luck.

Was written onto the yard roll as a native body by a clerk working from the wrong column, discovered the error eleven weeks later, and has been an unpaid irregular at her own trade ever since, because the guild pays visitors and there is no line in its book for her.

personality.summary: Methodical to the point of dullness on the bench and unexpectedly stubborn off it. She is not a woman searching for meaning; she is a woman who knows exactly what she proved, cannot use it, and has decided to be the last person alive who can still do the thing the proving came out of. She has no interest in being believed and a strong interest in being correct.
traits: can close a core into a closed shell to a tolerance she sets herself, and can name which graded punch does which width without looking at the set
formed and held a first closed centre with no shell of any kind, in a frame that was never adapted to anything, which makes her the only living control for the guild's entire founding premise

can build and repair a working face's closure, and knows that the flats cannot be surveyed, so every claim she makes about where a thing stands is proved by leaving a marker rather than by counting
mannerisms: runs a thumb along a finished edge instead of looking at it, and has to be told to stop by people who find it unnerving

answers a compliment about her work by describing the next thing that will need doing, which in this yard is usually worse than what she has just finished
motivations: wants the last cager's tools kept working, and will teach somebody if the guild will let her teach somebody
wants the finding about the caging written down in a place that outlives her, and has twice been refused a plate because the guild's book records its title and not its arguments
wants to know whether an unadapted frame is the reason her gate closed or whether she simply got lucky, and has nobody in the setting who could run the comparison
wants the yard to be able to pay her, and has never once asked, on the grounds that asking would be asking to be paid for a finding
flaws: has known for four years that her gate closed without ore and has said so to exactly four people, all of whom had reasons not to publish it
assumes the finding is worthless because it is worth nothing to the only institution that could act on it, and has not once considered that it might be worth something to a different one
took the caging trade because it was the trade the yard would take her, and has built an entire professional identity on a craft whose premise has been falsified by her own body
has stayed at the bench through four years of doing nothing there, because leaving would mean saying out loud that there is no more material, which is the guild's announcement to make and not hers
personality.voice: Level, unhurried, and mostly about widths, temperatures and closures. She uses the yard's vocabulary exactly as she was taught it and does not extend it, so she sounds more provincial than she is. She has a habit of answering a philosophical question with a workshop observation and then catching herself doing it. She does not raise her voice and has never once been described as arguing.
taboos: will not take a payment that is described as a retainer rather than as a wage, on the grounds that a retainer can be ended without an argument
will not open the core under her own collarbone for an examiner, and has refused twice in writing
will not describe the fourth gate as closed, only as unreached, because the difference is the only thing she has left to be accurate about
will not teach the caging to anybody who has not first watched a plate split, which has narrowed her candidates to almost nobody

relationships.note: The body everybody is born into before the world has an opinion about them, stopping where mortals stop and lending no discipline, which is exactly why it is weak and why it must settle on a path early. Its mind path is closed outright. What it has instead of specialisation is the absence of any prior composition at all, and a core forms at the one place a frame can first be built around something other than habit, so an unadapted frame is the easiest body in the setting to build a gate into and the weakest at everything that follows.

A dense core forms where the ribs meet the spine, and it is the first place the body can be built around something other than habit. The closing chance is low enough that the figures call the attempt a gamble and the yard's foreman had put money on her not managing it. She closed it cleanly with nothing in the building to hold it, which is the only clean close of that gate on the flats that anybody alive can point to, and it is also the only one nobody has been willing to publish.

The mortal tier's only dense material and the only thing on this tier a body can be caged in, scarce for two compounding reasons: the seam is worked out and a world with no spatial law cannot open a fresh one, so the exhaustion is permanent rather than a supply problem. The market has no instrument for a good that may end entirely, so the last of it is not expensive but unobtainable, which are different states. The next material that will cage a body lies above the spirit tier, so the ladder has no rung between.

Realms three and four, when the ladder's first genuine bottleneck turned out to be metallurgy, because a core has to be caged in something and the only dense material on the plains was iron ore. That era named itself for the difficulty and then built a four-generation craft to answer it. Her body answers it in a sentence and cannot be used, because the answer is that the cage was not the mechanism, and there is nothing left for a mechanism-shaped question to be pointed at.

When the seam ran out the tier lost its whole remaining ladder at once: cores stopped forming, the fourth gate became unreachable, and everyone standing above the second starved where they stood. She was above the second, and did not, and the only available explanation is the one nobody at the guild will put in a book, which is that her gate did not require the material that killed everyone else who was standing in the same place.

The frame carries itself there, a shape that holds without the will that learned it holding, and nothing elemental and nothing spatial is licensed on this band, so a body practitioner cannot reach for an effect the three slots simply do not hold. It became unreachable when the seam went and has been unreachable on this tier ever since, so she is currently the last commonborn on the plains standing above the gate where the whole disaster is supposed to have stopped everybody, and she has not yet worked out what to do about that.

reference_stats.summary: A generalist body on a ladder built for specialists, currently stopped at a gate that stopped the entire tier, and the only person alive whose frame contradicts the founding premise of the guild that employs her. She is not a fighter. She is a competent tradesperson in a yard with nothing to trade, who happens to be carrying the one clean result the yard's whole history was aimed at.
strengths: holds a closed centre in her own frame with no shell, which no technique, form or stance in the setting addresses because nothing in the ladder assumes it can exist
is unadapted, which makes her the easiest frame on the flats to seat a gate into and the easiest to read, because there is nothing in her for a technique to catch on first
can close and repair a face's shell to a tolerance she sets herself and can name which punch is which width without looking
is native to the tier, which means no boundary, stair, gate or crossing can refuse her, and the passage that is the setting's only durable wealth cannot be levied against her in the usual way
has said almost nothing about her own gate for four years and has therefore never once been contradicted on the record
weaknesses: lends no discipline whatsoever, so she is weakest precisely where a specialist is strongest and every gate above the third will cost her more than it costs anybody else
is closed to the mind path outright, so there is no version of her that answers from the inside or works on anybody through attention
has no certified gate beyond the second and no published record of the third, so every form and stance the ladder sells is formally unavailable to her and formally deniable if she uses one
has no lawful reason to be at a working face, because the tier licenses no native body for the work, so her presence is a clerical error rather than an employment
spends four years at a bench with nothing to work on, and a body that lends no discipline gets no better at waiting
reference_stats.combat_read: She should not be in a fight and would say so. Nothing she owns reaches anybody quickly, and a commonborn frame is weak in exactly the places a specialist frame is not, which means the correct read is to decline. The one thing worth knowing is that nothing in the cultivation ladder has a technique addressed to an uncaged core, so a practitioner who has read anything at all about what she is carrying will have no answer at all, and will reach for the nearest available one, which will be the wrong one. She is not dangerous. She is unaddressable, and in a fight that occasionally amounts to the same thing.
notes: Her one proven finding is worth more than the entire remaining stock of the only dense material on the tier, and the guild cannot act on it because its title is to that stock.
The third gate's closing chance is low and the yard's own figures call it a gamble, which means her result is also the only clean close of that gate anywhere on the flats.
She is an unpaid irregular at her own trade because the guild's wage table is written for visitors arriving down the stair and has no line for a body born on the flats.
Every measurement on the flats is proved by leaving a marker rather than by counting a distance, so there is no way for anybody to check where her bench is.

art.palette_notes: Oxide red-brown, iron grey, unbleached canvas, with the seam key's hard orange as the single saturated value and it worn close to the body. She is deliberately painted to sit inside the palette of the yard: the same reds and greys as the ground, the same value range as the bench and the plates, so that in any yard composition she reads as part of the equipment. Hard-edged contact shadow only at the boots and under the bench, no cast shadow. Ink contours even and unhurried rather than heavy, wash in flat blocks with the ore fines left as an unmixed speckle across the whole figure.
