identity.realm: Eleventh gate, Spirit Manifestation, on the body path. That gate is the first at which a dense composition can be read from outside at all — the frame prints its own outline in the law values it sits in — so it is the only rung of her ladder that makes her measurable, and she got there by being the guild's control without knowing it was one. Three gates short of a ceiling that every dense frame in the record shares and that nobody has explained since.

appearance.presentation: A large, slow, granite-coloured woman who looks like a piece of the guild's own masonry that has been kept warm. She is dressed identically to every member in the immersion cut and identically to every member in working clothes, and the sameness is a rule rather than an indifference. She is easy to find in a crowd and impossible to tell from the crowd at a glance.
appearance.age: Eighty-eight, in a hundred-and-forty-eight-year frame that is not deteriorating and will not be getting any harder. She has kept the immersion count for thirty-one years and has held the guild's frame tally for eleven.
appearance.build: Enormous, broad through the chest and hips, with a skeleton visibly heavier than anything else she works beside and forearms she can close both hands around at once. Slow. Nothing about her is graceful and she has stopped apologising for it in about the year it stopped being noticed.
appearance.complexion: Grey-pale and faintly mottled, like stone left near damp. It does not flush and it takes a bruise for weeks. Under immersion it goes a shade darker and stays that way for an hour afterwards, which is the single visible event her whole practice produces on her and which the guild has never once counted as a result.
appearance.hair: Coarse, iron-grey, worn in a single heavy knot at the nape and kept out of the water by an oiled band. It is the same cut every member of the guild wears because the guild wrote the instruction once and copied it for generations and nobody in it has the standing to modernise anything.
appearance.eyes: Grey, slow, and set deep under a heavy brow, with the pale ring the guild's cold habit leaves under the lower lid. She watches a thing for a long time before looking at it and is genuinely unaware of doing it, which the immersion count depends on entirely.
appearance.palette: Wet stone grey, bone, and undyed wool, with the guild's two accents and no more: the rust-red of a worked iron tie and the cold blue-black of immersion water. She is painted inside the guild's own palette so that a hall full of members reads as one material, and the only value in any composition of hers that is not in the building is the water.
appearance.attire: Heavy layered wool cut for cold immersion, cut to be removed instantly and worn with every fastening permanently undone at the collar and cuffs for exactly that reason. High collar, long sleeves, covered shoulders, nothing open at the neck. Soft-soled boots resoled to nothing. An oined cloth band at the hair, a guild tally board slung at the hip on a strap, and a leather apron over the top for working days that is the only garment she owns which is not guild-issued.
appearance.marks: A pale ring under each lower lid from thirty-one years of immersion, a hard thickened ridge across both knuckles where she takes a member's elbow to steady them in the water, and the faint even outline of her own composition showing through the skin at the collarbone — the only external reading her frame gives, and the reason she can be measured at all.
appearance.bearing: Immovable and unhurried, and the stillness is structural rather than chosen: a frame this dense does not shift its weight quickly, so a person watching her for a while concludes she is calmer than she is. In the water she is the only member who never moves first, and she holds that position by not moving at all rather than by effort.

canon.role_in_story: The Stonewright guild holds itself together with a cold practice that hardens bone and closes the meridians against strain, in bodies that were never designed to take the meridian burn the qi path uses, and it bought itself a second and shorter ladder in that currency. The currency is the immersion, and it is spent by being spent: a member who has had a season of it has a closed meridian and a harder frame and cannot have the old one back. So the whole institution is denominated in a thing that is consumed by the act of receiving it, and it needs to know whether it is receiving it. She is the answer. A stoneborn is the densest body in the record and the density is the same property that closes what the practice closes, so on her frame the immersion produces no before and no after and the guild's one social test — every member immerses in company and nobody leaves the water first — has nothing to be a test of. She is the only stoneborn the guild has ever measured before and after by the same hand, because she is the only one it has ever been able to measure at all: she stands at the eleventh gate, which is the first gate on that ladder at which a dense composition can be read from outside at all, the frame printing its own outline in the law values it sits in. Eleven years of readings say the same thing every time. The guild cannot publish that, because a house that cannot certify its own work cannot admit a member whose presence makes the work uncertifiable. The guild cannot retire her, because the roll is the roll, and refusing an immersion in company is the culture's first taboo, and she is the one member the water will not change. So she has been the control for a third of a century without ever being told she is one, while the tally board at her hip has recorded every immersion day the guild has run and has never once had a column for what any of them achieved.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing waist-deep at the far end of the immersion cut with both hands on the frame, absolutely motionless while eleven other members come and go around her, and being asked — by a new apprentice, not by anybody senior — whether anything is supposed to happen, and answering that she has been asked that four times and that the honest answer is that she does not know.
canon.lore: A stoneborn is a dense, slow body assembled for load-bearing work. It carries more physique and stamina than anything else in the setting and it stops at the immortal tier, because the density that makes it durable is the same density that will not let a dantian form; the mind path is closed to it outright, for the same reason. That single property is the whole of the guild's founding. A fixed dense frame can carry and lift in a way nothing else here can, and the same density closes what a qi technique needs open, so this culture bought its members a second ladder, shorter than the real one, in a currency no other body has: cold. Immersion hardens bone and closes the meridians against strain, the guild's year is counted in immersion days and nothing else, and the practice has a taboo attached to describing it as hardening, because nothing in the body asked to be hardened — a body that cannot be changed by qi was given a second method, not a nature. On a commonborn apprentice the method visibly does something. On a stoneborn it does nothing at all, and the reason is the guild's own founding premise: the density was already there. She is not, by any measure the guild possesses, an unsuccessful immersion. She is a body the practice was not designed for, standing in it. And she happens to be the only member whose frame can be read from the outside at all. That gate is a diagnostic and not an attack: a dense enough composition prints its own outline in the law values it sits in, and it is the first gate on the body ladder that needs a law group the path does not itself read. Above it, at the top of the ladder, the densest frames become indistinguishable from the matter around them, which the record calls convenient and unprovable — a body that complete has no external reading to test it against. So her species is legible for exactly the band she occupies and blind above it and blind below it, and she occupies the legible band by accident, having gone looking for a gate that would let somebody finally measure her and found one that instead made her measurable in the one respect nobody wanted. The guild's etiquette is that a builder does not accept a compliment and returns it as a measurement, because the culture has no way to praise something that is not also a specification for the next one. That rule is the reason eleven years of a null result cannot be said out loud. A null result is not a measurement. It is the absence of one, and there is no form of words in this guild for the absence of one.
history: Bred into a guild household at birth and put into the immersion cut at nine years old, on the same terms as every commonborn apprentice on the roll, because the guild's admission rite does not distinguish and its own counts show commonborn apprentices outnumbering stoneborn members more than two to one.

Closed the eleventh gate at fifty-seven, on a worked face on the spirit-tier grounds, and found that for the first time in her life something outside her own body could be read — the frame prints its own outline — and that she immediately and privately began using it on other people rather than on herself.

Started keeping the immersion count at fifty-seven, because the clerk who held it left for the stair and nobody replaced him, and discovered in the first winter that a day is counted by immersion and not by attendance, so a member who stood in the shallows for a quarter of a bell is entered identically to one who stayed.

Began the before-and-after readings at seventy-seven, on her own initiative and without being asked, because she was the only member whose frame could be read from outside and it had never occurred to anybody that this made her a control rather than a subject.

Was asked by four separate apprentices across eleven years what is supposed to happen, and has answered all four the same way, and has told precisely one member of the guild the whole of the result, who is the third head and who has said nothing at all about it since.

personality.summary: Enormous, unhurried, and privately certain that the guild's currency does not work on her and publicly unable to say so in any form the guild would accept. She keeps a count nobody has audited, holds a position nobody has authorised, and has spent eleven years turning a finding into a tally because a tally is a thing her culture has a column for and a finding is not.
traits: holds a fixed position in moving water for longer than the culture's own social test requires, without effort, because a frame this dense does not drift
prints her own composition in the law values she sits in, which makes her externally readable to any instrument and the only member of the guild who can be measured at all
produces no measurable change under the guild's entire currency, and has verified this herself thirty-one times in a row, by hand, at the same hour
carries more physique and stamina than anything else in the setting and is correspondingly slow, and has made the slowness into a service rather than an excuse
keeps the guild's immersion count exactly, including the days she knows should not have been counted and counted anyway
mannerisms: takes a member's elbow to steady them in the water without being asked and without looking at them
answers any compliment about her work by handing back a measurement of the next job, because the culture has no other form available
watches a thing for a long time before looking at it, which the count depends on and which she has never noticed doing
stands at the far end of the cut with her hands on the frame, in the one position in the guild that nobody thinks of as occupied
says the word for the practice as the guild's instructions say it, and will not use a plainer word for it, and will not explain the refusal
motivations: wants the guild to be able to certify its own currency, and has concluded that the only route to that is a measurement rather than a conviction, and there is nothing left to measure
wants the third head to put a sentence about the readings in the guild book, having concluded that she is not going to be asked twice

wants one more gate above the eleventh, where the frame becomes indistinguishable from the matter around it and there is finally no external reading to contradict her, and knows that wanting that is wanting to be unprovable
wants to be released from the immersion, and has worked out that the guild's first taboo makes her the only member who can be neither given it nor allowed to refuse it
flaws: has spent eleven years collecting a null result and calling it a tally, which is a way of not saying the sentence that the tally implies
is so certain she is right that she has never asked whether the readings are wrong, which is the one hypothesis eleven years of identical results has not excluded
answers every question about her own frame by returning a measurement, which is a guild rule she has adopted so thoroughly that she can no longer report a feeling at all
has let the third head know, and has let nobody else know, and has noticed that this makes her complicit rather than careful
personality.voice: Low, slow, and made almost entirely of quantities and dates. She names immersion days rather than seasons and counts them out loud under her breath when she thinks nobody is listening. She does not use contractions, does not finish other people's sentences, and has never been described as complaining. When she cannot answer a question she says so in the guild's own trade words and then stands there.
taboos: will not describe the cold practice as hardening, or as anything else, including when directly asked by an apprentice
will not leave the water first, and has never once done so, including on the day she entered it and including when ill
will not enter a reading in the tally board that she has not taken herself with her own hand
will not accept a compliment about the count, and returns it as a discrepancy every time without exception

relationships.note: A dense, slow body assembled for load-bearing work, carrying more physique and stamina than anything else in the setting and stopping at the immortal tier because the density that makes it durable is the same density that will not let a dantian form. Its mind path is closed outright for the same reason. She is the only reason the guild that built a second ladder in cold exists at all, and she is also the body the second ladder cannot be spent on.

A guild of builders held together by a cold practice that hardens bone and closes the meridians against strain, in bodies never designed to take the meridian burn the qi path uses, because the density that lets a frame carry and lift is the same density that closes what a qi technique needs open. The culture's etiquette is that a builder does not accept a compliment but returns it as a measurement, because it has no way to praise something that is not also a specification. That rule is why eleven years of a null result cannot be stated: a null result is not a measurement, and the guild has no form of words for the absence of one.

The body can be read from outside at this gate: a dense enough composition prints its own outline in the law values it sits in. It is a diagnostic rather than an attack and the first gate on the body ladder that needs a law group the path does not itself read. She cleared it looking for a way to be measured at all, and found the one gate that measures her in exactly the respect nobody wanted measured. Above this band the densest frames become indistinguishable from the matter around them, which is convenient and unprovable, so her species is legible in one narrow place on the whole ladder and she is standing in it.

It hardens the outer frame until qi runs along it like wire, and it is half elemental, so the form holds against wood and cracks against fire. It is the most direct expression of the guild's entire currency in the form tree, and on her frame there is nothing left for it to do, because the hardening it performs is the property her species was assembled out of. A guild that charges its members for a hardening has no way to charge her, and has never once written down what it does instead.

The body's answer to the qi path's void is subtraction, spent removing everything in the composition that is not load bearing, because a dense frame has no room for filler and filler is what fails first under a law value pressed past its range. This is the one gate on her ladder that a dense frame is genuinely well suited to, and it is also the gate where the reason becomes clearest: there is no filler in her. The gate has nothing to remove and she has nothing to gain by removing it.

The densest bodies in the setting stop at realm seventeen, one gate short of the end of their own tier, and nobody has explained it since; the era that produced it was the one frame with a complete composition and no redundancy, which is the frame in which a fixed dense body has nothing left to form. The ceiling is still there and is still unexplained by anyone who was not there. She is three gates short of it and is the only dense frame in her guild who has ever asked to be left alone near it, because above her current gate the readings stop.

reference_stats.summary: The most durable body in the setting, on a ladder built for a currency her frame was born holding, at the one gate that lets her be measured at all and cannot measure the thing anybody wanted. She is slow, enormous, almost impossible to move and has no technique in the tree that does anything to her. What she offers is that she can stand in one place for as long as the job takes and be entirely unaffected by whatever the water is doing to everybody else.
strengths: cannot be moved, hurried, leaned on or crowded, because the frame that makes her durable is the frame that makes her immovable
prints her own composition in the law values she sits in, so any instrument can read her state without her cooperation and without being able to be lied to
closes and holds the meridians against strain for free, since the density already does what the guild's currency is bought to do
carries more than anything else in the setting and can do it repeatedly, so any position that must be held can be held by her indefinitely
cannot form a dantian and therefore cannot be compelled, pacified, instructed or frightened by anything that works through cultivation
weaknesses: is at the eleventh gate and three gates short of a ceiling that every dense frame shares and nobody has explained, so her remaining ladder is finite and shared
moves slowly enough that a lighter body can simply leave, and has no technique in the tree that reaches anybody first
is closed to the mind path outright, so nothing she does can be aimed at anybody's attention and nothing aimed at hers can get in
produces no change under the guild's currency, which makes her institutionally useless in the one practice that holds it together
holds a position in moving water by not moving, which fails entirely the moment the ground she is standing on is what is moving
reference_stats.combat_read: She is a wall and not a duellist, and the correct read is to refuse the engagement rather than to solve her. Nothing she owns travels quickly, nothing she owns discourages an approach, and no technique in the ladder has an answer to a frame with no dantian in it, because there is nothing to reach through. The genuinely dangerous thing about her is positional and administrative: she can hold a doorway, a corridor, a cut in a wall or an immersion for as long as the job takes, and a body that cannot be moved is a piece of ground that cannot be taken. Attacking her directly is expensive, slow and pointless. If she must be displaced, the answer is the ground under her rather than the body on it.
notes: Her frame is externally readable only in a narrow band of the ladder, and only in the band she happens to occupy, and the reading gives away nothing she would want concealed and everything the guild would want published.
The immersion count is kept by immersion and not by attendance, so she has counted days she knows should not have qualified.
She has verified her own null result thirty-one times by hand at the same hour and has never tested the one hypothesis that would explain it.

Every member of her guild including the commonborn apprentices has received something from the practice she cannot receive, which is the reason the guild is not a study in failure and she is not a study in anything.

art.palette_notes: Wet stone grey, bone and undyed wool, deliberately inside the guild's own material palette so that any group of members reads as one substance rather than as a crowd of people. Two accents only: rust-red on a worked iron tie, and cold blue-black in the water. Hard-edged contact shadow where the body meets the cut floor and nowhere else, no cast shadow, no bloom in the water. Ink contours enormously heavy and doubled along the outer silhouette, the guild's own habit of showing the structure; wash laid in flat blocks with visible dry-brush at every edge and the pale external outline of the composition left as an unpainted lighter line under the skin.
